output.summary: KEP-2887 adds a `+enum` marker on Go type aliases so the Kubernetes OpenAPI generator can detect and emit enum values for string-typed fields, applied to built-in types. The KEP is at stage beta with status implementable.
output.rationale: Enum-like fields in the core API are plain strings, so their allowed values are documented in comments and duplicated in validation code, and UIs cannot show dropdowns. The KEP proposes a marker that the OpenAPI generator reads to deduce values from the Go type definition, with all built-in enums annotated. Reviewers raised concerns about closed-enum forward/backward compatibility and kubebuilder divergence, and the discussion records that clients should treat enums as open.

alternatives.option: Keep enum types as plain strings with comment-only documentation
alternatives.why_not: The KEP states the problem: values are duplicated across the code base and tools cannot show dropdowns. The sources do not record a rejection of this option beyond that.

alternatives.option: Implement the feature in OpenAPI v2 as well
alternatives.why_not: The Drawbacks section says the breaking effect on users expecting plain strings is 'the main reason for not implementing this feature in OpenAPI v2'. A reviewer also suggested the v2 improvement could be delivered separately from OpenAPI v3.

alternatives.option: Require kubebuilder support for the marker before merging
alternatives.why_not: Reviewers (sttts) asked for kubebuilder support as a goal and requirement. The author responded that kubebuilder would be supported too, and the sources do not show this was made a blocking prerequisite.

evidence.quote: This KEP proposes a `+enum` marker to type aliases that represent enums. The OpenAPI generator will have the capability to recognize the marker and auto-detect possible values for an enum.
This KEP will break any users that expect enum types to be plain strings. This is the main reason for not implementing this feature in OpenAPI v2
They are closed from a server-side perspective (server won't allow any unknown value). Clients, for backwards compatibility reasons, should consider it open (new values are possible).
I opened https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/109177 to track an issue with forward-compatibility of generated clients using language-level enums.
Let's hold on to GA this one for one more release while the dust settles.
